I think BJJ is very good for self defense, but I do not think it is the best martial art. I think judo is the best for self defense as it gives you a better ability to put yourself in a position to control the fight's location with throws, and throws onto things like concrete and pavement hurt a lot. It will also teach you enough grappling skills to easily outclass someone without any experience, granted it usually will leave you with a large discrepancy against a BJJ practitioner.

I believe that a large reason to why people seem to think striking techniques are better for self-defense is because they are shown so effectively in movies. You can tag someone who is significantly better than you. I did that the first time I tried boxing. I have used BJJ in self-defense and I believe it works well.

I manage a small shop in a pedestrian mall. When we are open we put about a third of our stock out the front of the shop. It's completely obvious if we're open or not but just in case we put 'We're open, come on in!' sign on the door.

We opened at 8:30 as normal this morning. Pot plants, garden furniture and ornaments lined the front of the shop. The lights were on. Three staff were working. Customers in and out as normal. I had forgotten to put the sign up on the door, but it was completely obvious we were open. Completely.

A lady rang about 10:30 to ask if we were open, and I said we were until 5:30. She thanked me and said that she wasn't sure as there was no sign on the door. I didn't really think anything of it and went on with things. I didn't put the sign on the door as I'm lazy and couldn't be bothered.

A lady rang about 10:35 to ask if we were open - the same lady. She shouted that she was confused if the shop was open or not as there was no sign on the door. I was about to do my best retail non-apology when a customer came in and I heard the shouting through the open door. The lady was standing about 5m from the shop. I walked out to her and killed her with retail kindness, asking if she wanted anything in particular, offering to show her the specials etc.

The lady then said that she didn't actually need anything for her garden, she just thought it was unprofessional not to have a sign. There was a bit of shouting about it. I thanked her for her suggestion as politely as I could and went back to the shop.

I didn't put up the sign though, I don't want the terrorists to win.
